result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives full per-script stacks with system fallbacks, shows how Latin stop names in Arabic and Japanese are handled, and tells the reader to test with the web fonts blocked and on real devices. A has solid advice on optical matching and on mixed-script runs. However, its single font stack has no per-platform fallbacks, it says little about gaps between devices, and it drifts into general layout topics such as logical properties, icon mirroring and line wrapping. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A gives separate per-language stacks with system fallbacks for each script. Its Latin-first ordering keeps embedded stop names in the same letterforms, and it explains how to fix size if they look small next to kanji. B covers similar ground, but its single combined stack has no system fallbacks, and it drifts into general RTL layout and line-breaking advice. Neither answer says much about platform gaps on system fonts.
